newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks set record after dollar rally.
newsitem.headline: French stocks set record after dollar rally.

text.p: French stocks set a new closing record on Friday after an advance fuelled by the dollar's strength.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 52.41 points, or 1.76 percent, at 3,025.94, surpassing its last closing record, set on Wednesday, of 3,003.53 points.
It hit an all time intraday high of 3,030.62 on Friday.
"We're being pulled up by the dollar and by the government's pragmatism on the euro that has reassured the markets," a broker said.
The CAC-40 July futures contract rose 49 points to 3,028.

PSA Peugeot Citroen shares rose 7.25 percent to 695 francs, their highest level this year, after brokerage Cheuvreux de Virieu raised its rating on the stock to buy from sell, underscoring a shift in sentiment on the French car sector due in part to favourable currency movements. Renault rose 1.62 percent. It hit a year high on Wednesday.

LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton shares underperformed, climbing 1.05 percent to 1,629 francs, after a rejection from Guinness and Grand Metropolitan to the French group's proposal for a three-way drinks merger.
LVMH said it would continue pushing the merits of its plan to other shareholders in the British groups.
Guinness's chairman signalled that the British were still open to negotiations.
